position_in_era.historical_role: Early template for the aria↔solo dialectic: Ritchie Blackmore's escalating guitar solo and Ian Gillan's banshee falsetto scream cycle through the song in counterpoint, each amplifying the other's intensity.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded 4 December 1969 at IBC Studios, London. Jon Lord's organ riff, acknowledged by Ian Gillan as based on It's a Beautiful Day's 1969 song 'Bombay Calling', anchors the composition. Blackmore's guitar and Gillan's voice engage in call-and-response cycles across 10+ minutes.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Blackmore and Gillan as competing protagonists: Blackmore's slow-building solo escalates to frenzied runs before abruptly stopping; Gillan's falsetto screams answer and match the guitar's intensity. Neither occupies the foreground alone for long.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Ritchie Blackmore – lead guitar (Gibson SG); Jon Lord – Hammond organ; Ian Gillan – vocals; Roger Glover – bass; Ian Paice – drums. Lord's organ is the structural spine; Blackmore and Gillan are the dual foreground voices.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: In Rock marked Deep Purple Mk II's breakthrough. 'Child in Time' became the centrepiece of their live set, often stretching beyond 15 minutes with extended Blackmore–Gillan duels.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Album released June 1970 (UK). The song's Cold War-themed lyrics ('Sweet child in time, you'll see the line') contextualise the urgency of Gillan's screams.
